technical.title: Structured prompting with role, task, context, format
technical.summary: Compose prompts that specify the assistant's role, the task, relevant context, and the expected output format. Claude-specific: use <context>/<task>/<format> XML tags for complex requests.

technical.title: Reason about context windows and token budgets
technical.summary: Understand when a request is too long, when to chunk, and how to use retrieval instead of jamming everything into context.

technical.title: Use AI to summarise policy and regulation
technical.summary: Municipal / parish administrators can summarise long regulatory texts quickly with AI — always link to the authoritative source.

critical.title: Detect and verify claims that sound confident but may be hallucinated
critical.summary: Cross-check specific numbers, quotes, and citations against primary sources. Treat unverified facts as a red flag.

critical.title: Ask for confidence and act accordingly
critical.summary: Prompt for explicit uncertainty signals and treat hedged AI output as hedged — don't collapse it into a single certain answer.

critical.title: AI must not be the final voice to constituents
critical.summary: A public servant remains accountable. AI drafts, humans sign.

ethical.title: Respect data-sharing boundaries
ethical.summary: Know what you can and cannot paste into a third-party AI tool. Default to anonymising PII, PHI, and proprietary data.

ethical.title: Recognise and counter training-data bias
ethical.summary: Ask the model to consider alternative perspectives and to flag when its training data may be incomplete or skewed.

ethical.title: Disclose AI use in public-sector deliverables
ethical.summary: Public trust requires transparency about when and how AI was used.

domainSpecific.title: Casework and constituent-communication AI
domainSpecific.summary: Many LA parish and state offices are piloting AI summarisation of casework; learn the deployed tool.

recommendedModules.rationale: Ground how LLMs actually generate text before trusting them at work.
Structured prompting is the highest-leverage skill for anyone using AI.
Hallucinations, bias, and data-handling rules matter in every regulated workplace.
